items.title: 68516_Gene Ramey oral history interview
items.q: No. One thing before, when I knew him, you'd see him drunk in the afternoon, like that.

ctx.x: the big band and the small.

He -- he was a man that could play a thing. And there was a man -- we forgot he could play both -- a guy in Paris, lives over there now -- what's his name? Kenny Clarke -- Clarke, yeah, Klook Clarke, we call him, yeah, Kenny Clarke.

But now that thing, I still have to go back to Sonny Greer and Jo Jones, Crawford and those cats that made that rhythm section, pop, you know. They heard everything that the brass was doing. They knew how to bring the band up. You know, that first chorus, that rhythm section is not going to play that second chorus like he did that first chorus. They play that first chorus more or less and let that, especially the soloist find himself, give him a chance to relax, but that second chorus, they were supposed to blow…
